static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.family_status: Living alone, with no immediate family members
static_traits.social_status: Has friends in the ballet circle, but has not yet discussed specific feelings with them
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past; no psychotherapy received; no significant physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Neutral tone, clear expression, able to self-reflect; tending to narrate around negative details

basic_info.main_problem: After a mistake in a recent ballet performance, continuously experiencing disappointment and failure, repeatedly dwelling on the error while ignoring successful parts of the performance, affecting the overall view of the ballet career and emotional state; also strong Anxiety and Self-denial from a financial-management mistake.
basic_info.core_demands: Hopes to relieve the disappointment and sense of failure surrounding performance mistakes and financial errors, and restore her passion for ballet and overall mental health.

core_beliefs: Only a perfect performance counts as competent

special_situations.event: During last month's ballet performance, a slipping mistake occurred
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as one mistake occurs in the performance, the whole performance equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to relieve negative emotions by rationalizing and reminding self of the positive parts of performing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This slip ruined the whole performance; I am a failure

special_situations.event: Whenever thinking of that performance or practicing for an upcoming performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by fixating on mistakes and ignoring successes can I avoid making mistakes again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly recalling that mistake while overlooking success fragments
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That mistake shows I am not good enough, other performances do not matter

special_situations.event: Self-evaluating after a performance with overall good showing
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Positive parts do not count, any mistake can undo all achievements
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating and ignoring positive feedback and successful segments, to stay vigilant about errors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That one mistake undid all my achievements

special_situations.event: Facing a new financial decision after a stock loss
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One investment failure means I am unsuited for financial management, and will keep failing in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly looking through financial-management strategies and seeking advice in forums, second-guessing and hesitating over every decision
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I ruined my financial future; every decision will become a disaster

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain others' affirmation and self-security through stable, error-free performance and sound decisions
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated after mistakes, relationship estrangement, damaged career prospects and financial security
defense_goal: Preventing repeat failure with harsh self-demands and excessive reflection
Reducing Anxiety and uncertainty through intellectualization and information seeking

object_relations.self_representation: A not-competent-enough performer/decision-maker prone to errors
object_relations.object_representation: Others (peers, audience, evaluators) who might become disappointed and distant because of one's own mistakes

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to review specific mistakes and their impact and to explore related feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to view deep emotional experience as unnecessary or uneasy, believing rational analysis alone solves problems
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a calm, objective tone, focusing on facts and data, reducing the expression of emotional vocabulary and subjective feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Anticipating others' reactions when discussing performance reviews or financial decisions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Assuming others will equate one error with total failure and negate it
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States in a self-critical and guilty tone, attributing all responsibility for the problem to oneself, downplaying external factors.

manifestations: Living alone and not yet discussing specific feelings with friends
Relationships with peers strained by negative self-views
After the performance mistake, overall view of his ballet career worsens
Questioning future performances and career prospects

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeated hesitation and second-guessing in financial decisions
In performance evaluation, focuses excessively on mistakes and ignores successes
Frequent self-criticism (e.g., 'I am destined to fail')

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Takes the perfectionist rule 'one mistake = complete failure' as an absolute standard

positive_force: Staying competent and confident in other life areas (self-reported good performance at work and personal hobbies)
There is potential social support in the ballet circle (has friends to talk with)
Actively seeks counseling and information, has motivation to change
Fairly good self-reflection ability, willing to try cognitive restructuring and behavioral experiments
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking, mental filtering and negating the positive
Catastrophizing/predicting the future about financial decisions leads to high Anxiety and avoidance
Strong Self-denial and shame, equating one error with overall failure
Sleep and diet affected, increased physical and mental burden
Social support not yet fully utilized, living alone and avoiding discussing specific feelings with friends

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly ruminating on performance mistakes and negating successful segments
antecedent: When practicing for the upcoming performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized perfectionism and the 'one mistake = failure' cognitive bias, with mental filtering and negating the positive
target_behavior.function: Maintaining high vigilance about errors to avoid failing again (escaping uncertainty and Anxiety)
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased sense of self-worth, worsened low mood and Anxiety, damaged career enthusiasm

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive hesitation and avoidance in financial decisions (continual second-guessing)
antecedent: Facing new investment or financial decisions
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic and future-predicting negative cognition after one loss ('I ruined my financial future')
target_behavior.function: Escaping potential risks and failure to temporarily reduce Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased decision efficiency, increased stress, disturbed sleep

antecedent: Self-evaluating after a performance with overall good showing
Situations where others or oneself review the strengths of a performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Black-and-white thinking and the 'positive does not count' cognitive assumption
target_behavior.function: Maintains high standards and a sense of control to prevent complacency
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced self-motivation, declining career motivation and confidence, relationships with peers further strained
